newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX applauds UK's SIB review of copper market.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX applauds UK's SIB review of copper market.

text.p: New York Mercantile Exchange president Patrick Thompson said Britain's regulatory watchdog, the Securities and Investments Board, has conducted a thorough probe of the Sumitomo copper scandal, but stiffer LME regulations could have avoided the debacle.
"At least they identified the correct topics," Thompson told Reuters following a NYMEX luncheon during the Futures Industry Association conference here.
The topics included margining and over-use of credit, surveillance of participants in the market, price transparency and information sharing.
Thompson also released an October 15 letter from NYMEX to the SIB stating that the Sumitomo scandal warranted a close look at the regulatory structure under which the Japanese trading house operated.

Sumitomo Corp racked up $2.6 billion in losses from allegedly unauthorised copper dealings by its former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, who was arrested in Japan on suspicion of forgery earlier this week.
"To the extent that the review leads to changes that better protect world commerce, the SIB is to be applauded," NYMEX's letter stated.

The SIB is probing the copper market and British brokers who may be involved in the Sumitomo affair. The watchdog has also issued a questionnaire seeking industry views on whether the LME needed reforming.
"NYMEX is pleased to offer its views on how such improvements can be made," the letter stated.
NYMEX's COMEX division trades copper futures, which compete directly with the LME's flagship red metal contract.
"The Sumitomo affair was not merely a rogue trader exposing a weak internal control -- if indeed, it turns out that we are dealing with a rogue at all," the letter said.
The activities of Sumitomo's trader appeared to have had a direct impact on the copper price, the letter continued.
"However, in our view, indications point more to an actual or an attempted market manipulation that failed after years in the making," the NYMEX letter stated.
"Moreover, enormous financial losses at one firm expose the world financial community to systemic financial stress of default even at marketplaces trading unreleated commodities."
"LME failed to provide meaningful systems to alert, and possibly avoid, the calamitous losses that happened here," the NYMEX letter said.
COMEX's concern with respect to the lack of transparency in LME prices has become far more accute by the addition of U.S. delivery locations in its copper contract.
"The review does a good job of identifying differences among regulatory regimes," NYMEX's letter concluded.
